title: London rental market activity rises post-legislation
summary:
London's rental market has shown resilience following the introduction of the Renters' Rights Act, with new data indicating continued activity despite regulatory changes. Foxtons reports new property listings increased 3.7% year-on-year in April 2026, while applicant registrations rose 9.5% as the market entered the spring letting season.

The post London rental market activity rises post-legislation appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Nuneaton council refunds £259k over unlawful empty homes tax
summary:
Nuneaton and Bedworth Borough Council has refunded more than £250,000 to owners of empty properties after admitting it failed to follow proper procedures before introducing higher council tax charges. The refunds followed an investigation which found the authority had not properly approved the scheme or fully assessed its impact on residents and the local economy.

title: Homeowners use AI to question agent valuations post-visit
summary:
Property sellers are increasingly using artificial intelligence tools to clarify and question estate agent valuations after market appraisal appointments, according to data from proptech firm Acaboom. The company analysed hundreds of anonymised interactions showing that more than half of all queries related to pricing, fees, marketing or contractual clarification.

title: Lloyds Banking Group considers ending Halifax brand
summary:
Lloyds Banking Group is evaluating plans to phase out the Halifax brand, potentially ending the 173-year-old banking and mortgage provider's operations as a standalone entity. The banking group is reportedly considering retiring Halifax this summer as part of ongoing consolidation of its branch network and retail banking operations.

title: Gender discrimination in property sector examined by agents
summary:
Gender discrimination and workplace barriers facing women in the property industry were examined in a recent podcast discussion featuring senior industry figures. The Estate Agent Showdown video series brought together agency leaders to discuss structural challenges women face in progressing through traditional agency models.

title: Four northern estate agents form collaboration network
summary:
Four independent estate and letting agents across northern England have established a collaboration network to share operational practices and serve landlords with multi-city portfolios. The network, named Centro, comprises firms managing over 2,000 residential properties across Leeds, Manchester, Liverpool and Newcastle.

title: Letting agents warned over legacy website content risks
summary:
Letting agents across England are being advised to conduct comprehensive reviews of their website content following the implementation of phase one of the Renters' Rights Act. Concerns have emerged that outdated material may remain accessible through search engine results despite updates to main website pages.

The post Letting agents warned over legacy website content risks appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Yorkshire agency launches second brand for wider market
summary:
A Yorkshire-based estate agency has launched a second trading brand to expand its services beyond the high-value residential market into lettings and property management. Child & Co Estates has been established by James and Steven Child, who founded Mr & Mr Child in May 2024.

The post Yorkshire agency launches second brand for wider market appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Avamore Capital completes £1.47m part-complete finance deal
summary:
Avamore Capital has provided a £1.47m development finance facility for a residential project that was already substantially advanced when the borrower sought refinancing. The transaction required the lender to assess work already completed and estimate remaining costs amid several complications.

The post Avamore Capital completes £1.47m part-complete finance deal appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: £3.5m finance secured for Ringwood Corn Exchange scheme
summary:
Pallas Capital has provided £3.54 million in development finance to support the conversion of The Corn Exchange in Ringwood, a building that has remained vacant for more than 20 years. The 18-month facility will fund 12 residential units alongside ground-floor and basement commercial space.
